questions.text: Under BP 344 and its 2024 Revised IRR, what is the maximum gradient permitted for an accessible ramp serving a heritage building entrance (where no mechanical alternative is feasible)?

options.text: 1:8 - permissible only for very short ramps under 1.5 m
1:12 - the previous standard retained in the 2024 IRR for heritage retrofits
1:20 - the checked BP 344 2024 IRR maximum (1:15 allowed only in special cases for shorter runs)
1:25 - preferred for landscaped approaches but not the regulatory maximum

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR Appendix A.1.1 (Accessible Ramps) states verbatim that ramps 'shall have... Gradient not steeper than 1:20. Steeper gradients may be allowed in special cases depending on the length to be covered.' Table A.1.1 lists 1:20 as the standard maximum (15 m landing interval) and 1:15 only for special cases (max length 10.50 m, max rise 700 mm, 10 m landing interval). The older 1:12 value is not the current 2024 IRR maximum for general accessible ramps. Heritage status does not relax BP 344 ramp gradient; where strict application is impossible, RA 10066 / NBC variance procedure with a documented cultural constraint and an alternative accessible route is the source-safe path, not a steeper ramp.

questions.text: During heritage building adaptive reuse, the architect finds the historic main entrance doorway is 750 mm wide - narrower than the BP 344 2024 Revised IRR minimum clear door width. What is the source-safe design response?

options.text: Accept the 750 mm doorway as-is because heritage buildings are automatically exempt from BP 344 accessibility standards
Demolish and rebuild the historic doorway to widen it to 900 mm regardless of cultural impact

File a variance request with the Building Official and NHCP documenting the cultural constraint and code impossibility, and provide an alternative accessible entrance (e.g., secondary door at 900 mm clear width or accessible route elsewhere)
Add a surface-mounted frame to narrow the doorway further to 'match' the historic opening

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR Appendix C.2 (Doors) states verbatim: 'All doors shall have a minimum clear width of 900 mm.' and 'For double-leaf doors, the minimum clear width shall be 1800 mm.' The historic 750 mm doorway is therefore non-compliant. Heritage status under RA 10066 does NOT automatically exempt the building from BP 344, but when code compliance directly conflicts with preservation (enlarging the historic doorway would destroy character-defining features), the source-safe response is to (1) file a variance request with the Building Official and NHCP documenting the cultural constraint and code impossibility, and (2) provide an alternative accessible entrance (secondary doorway meeting 900 mm clear width, or an accessible route elsewhere). Demolishing the historic fabric is a last resort, not the default; ignoring the requirement or further narrowing the doorway is non-compliant.
